name: PetMySite – Interactive Chat Button & Website Pet
author: petmysite

sections.description:
PetMySite replaces a plain chat bubble with a small animated pet, a friendly website mascot that sits in the corner of your website. Visitors tap the pet to open the live chat you already use, so there is no new inbox to learn.

PetMySite is a hosted service: you need a free PetMySite account, which you can create while connecting. Nothing is added to your website until an administrator connects it.

Highlights

  • Five pets to choose from: Piko, Dottie, Orbi, Wisp and Halo.
  • Opens Tawk.to, Crisp, Intercom / Fin or Zendesk Messaging, or a link of your choice.
  • Connect from Settings → PetMySite; there is no code to paste.
  • An optional [petmysite_launcher] shortcode adds an inline chat button to any page.
  • Respects reduced-motion preferences and pauses in hidden tabs.
  • The free plan includes every pet, chat and link actions and analytics; paid plans remove the small “by PetMySite” badge.

PetMySite for WordPress is a thin connector for the PetMySite hosted service. PetMySite keeps the chat provider you already use and supplies the hosted widget runtime, pet configuration, provider adapter, entitlement, and aggregate analytics services.

The plugin provides a secure PKCE connection flow, server-side connection checks, a connected-only loader for the hosted PetMySite runtime, and an optional inline launcher shortcode.

No PetMySite account password, Google credential, billing credential, or account-wide API token is stored in WordPress. After connection, WordPress retains only a public site key and a revocable site-scoped connector token.

The settings screen’s images, styles and fonts ship inside the plugin; it loads nothing from third-party CDNs. It bundles the Maven Pro and Manrope typefaces under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (see assets/fonts/OFL.txt).

External services

PetMySite is a hosted service provided at https://petmysite.com/.

After a site administrator explicitly connects this plugin to PetMySite, WordPress sends the site’s home URL, WordPress site URL, plugin version, PKCE challenge, and a one-time connection exchange to PetMySite. WordPress later uses a site-scoped token for status, verification, and disconnect requests. Connected public pages load the PetMySite widget runtime from PetMySite servers. The runtime retrieves public configuration for the connected hostname and may send privacy-friendly aggregate events such as widget impressions, pet interactions, and chat-open events.

PetMySite does not intentionally collect WordPress usernames, visitor identities, chat content, typed messages, or full page URLs as part of its widget analytics. The customer’s existing chat provider has its own independent privacy behavior.

Service: https://petmysite.com/

Privacy: https://petmysite.com/privacy

Terms: https://petmysite.com/terms
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin, search for “PetMySite”, then install and activate it.
  2. Open Settings → PetMySite and select Connect PetMySite.
  3. Sign in to PetMySite or create a free account, choose or create the site for this address, and return to WordPress.
  4. Open your website once so your pet can check in.
sections.faq:
Does PetMySite replace my live-chat provider?

No. PetMySite is designed to open the supported chat service already installed on the website.

Does this version add anything to the public website?

Nothing is added until an administrator completes the PetMySite connection. When connected and enabled, WordPress loads only the hosted pet.js runtime and the public site key. The secret connector token remains server-side.

How do I add an inline launcher?

Add [petmysite_launcher] or [petmysite_launcher label="Chat with us"] in any editor or builder that renders WordPress shortcodes.

Will the plugin ask me for a review?

Rarely, and only on the PetMySite settings screen. Two weeks after you connect, if your pet is live, the screen may ask for an honest review on WordPress.org. You can choose “Maybe later”, “I already did” or “Don’t ask again”; nothing is ever unlocked or withheld based on your answer.

How do I report a security issue?

Please email hello@petmysite.com with “Security” in the subject line and do not post details in the public support forum. We will confirm receipt and keep you updated while we investigate.

Where can I get help?

Open a topic in the support forum or visit the PetMySite help center.

What happens when I deactivate the plugin?

Deactivation retains local settings and the site connection so reactivation can resume safely. Deleting the plugin removes its local WordPress options and pending connection state.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4

  • Tell administrators when their chat provider wasn’t found on the website, so the pet’s chat actions never fail silently.
  • Disconnect always works, even after the website was removed from PetMySite or its WordPress address changed.
  • Shortcode buttons tell visitors when the pet can’t load instead of doing nothing.
  • Allow 30 minutes to create and verify a new PetMySite account while connecting.
  • A status check still running in another tab can no longer restore a connection you just disconnected.
  • Clean up records of abandoned connection attempts.

1.0.3

  • Ask administrators for an honest WordPress.org review two weeks after connecting, once their pet is live. The request can be snoozed or turned off and appears only on the PetMySite settings screen.
  • Redesign the settings screen before connecting: all five pets on an animated stage, a pet picker whose choice carries through to PetMySite, and clearer next steps.
  • Rename the connected screen’s main button to “Customize Your Pet” and sharpen the bundled pet images.
  • Point administrators to Settings → PetMySite until the site is connected, with a notice on the Plugins and Dashboard screens that can be dismissed.
  • Add help center and support forum links to the plugin’s row on the Plugins screen.
  • Improve the plugin description, installation steps, tags, screenshots and FAQ, including how to report a security issue.

1.0.2

  • Fix “Last checked” showing “Never” straight after connecting.
  • Refresh the status within a minute while the pet waits for its first visit, and suggest a check after previewing the site.
  • Keep the website address whole in the settings headline and move the connection steps below the banner.

1.0.1

  • Redesign the settings screen: a live status stage showing your pet, a setup checklist, readable connection details, a copyable launcher shortcode, and a two-step disconnect.
  • Open PetMySite pages from the settings screen in a new tab.
  • Bundle the settings screen’s images, styles and OFL fonts inside the plugin.

0.1.0

  • Add plugin lifecycle and per-site option storage.
  • Add strict settings and connection schemas.
  • Add public-key and connector-token validation.
  • Add short-lived, user-scoped PKCE state helpers.
  • Add the administrator connection, status, verification, and disconnect flow.
  • Load the hosted runtime only for valid, enabled connections.
  • Add the escaped [petmysite_launcher] shortcode.
